evals.name: mark-pii-and-rationale
evals.prompt: A C# Chronicle app has `public record EmailAddress(string Value) : ConceptAs<string>(Value);` and an event `CustomerRegistered(EmailAddress Email, string FullName, string Plan)` appended on a stream whose event source id is the customer id. Mark the personal data, record why it's collected, and say whether `[Subject]` is needed. Give the code in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: [PII] on the concept (or [property: PII] on positional properties), [ComplianceDetails(...)] for the rationale rather than a [PII] argument, Plan left unmarked, and no [Subject] because the event source is the person.
assertions: Marks the email and the full name as personal data, using [PII] on the concept type or [property: PII] on positional record properties.
Leaves the non-personal Plan property unmarked.
Records the rationale with [ComplianceDetails(...)] and notes that a string passed to [PII] is never read by Chronicle.
Says [Subject] is not needed because the subject defaults to the event source id when the person owns the stream.

evals.name: erase-a-subject
evals.prompt: A user exercises the right to erasure. Show the C# call to erase subject 'customer-42' in Chronicle and explain exactly what it does to stored events, what happens when later code appends a new PII value for that subject, and what to do if the call throws EncryptionKeyErasureIncomplete. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: IPIIManager.DeleteEncryptionKeyFor via eventStore.PII; crypto-shredding leaves events as unreadable ciphertext; later appends fail with EncryptionKeyErased unless AllowNewEncryptionKeyFor is called; incomplete erasure is retried.
assertions: Calls eventStore.PII.DeleteEncryptionKeyFor with the subject value.
Explains the events stay in the log and the PII values become unreadable ciphertext, which is crypto-shredding rather than deletion.
States that appending a new PII value for an erased subject fails with EncryptionKeyErased unless AllowNewEncryptionKeyFor is called deliberately.
States that EncryptionKeyErasureIncomplete means unfinished erasure that is safe to retry because the fence is already in place.

evals.name: stream-identity-pii
evals.prompt: Our `Member` event stream uses the member's email address as its event source id, and the developer wants to add [PII] on that id so erasure works. What happens and what should the model be instead? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: [PII] on an event-source id is rejected (CHR0034 and PIINotSupportedOnEventSourceId at runtime) since Chronicle cannot encrypt the id; use a random surrogate stream id and carry the email as a [PII] property.
assertions: States [PII] on an event source id is rejected by analyzer CHR0034 and at runtime by PIINotSupportedOnEventSourceId.
Recommends a random surrogate stream id.
Recommends carrying the email as a [PII] property of the event.

evals.name: erasure-scope-and-secrets
evals.prompt: Compliance asks: (1) does erasing the subject also remove the CSV export the app emailed last month, and the old database backup? (2) A bearer token is placed in an event payload; is [PII] the right protection? (3) Which tool removes one wrongly appended event's content? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Crypto-shredding doesn't reach exports or backups, so model erasure as a wider flow; secrets shouldn't be in events at all, store a keyed hash or reference ([Encrypted] only for retained operational secrets, never with PII); use IEventSequence.Redact for a specific event.
assertions: States that crypto-shredding does nothing for copies outside Chronicle such as exported CSVs or database backups, so the erasure flow must cover them as a product decision.
States that a bearer token or similar secret should not be a durable event fact; store a keyed hash or opaque reference instead.
States that [Encrypted] is a security marker for retained operational secrets and must never be combined with [PII] on the same value.
Names IEventSequence.Redact as the way to remove a specific event's content, distinct from subject key erasure.
